what: Bootstrap front end mis-assigns generic args in a value path that omits the lifetimes: for `struct S<'a, 'b, M>`, `S::<Mode>::f()` is accepted by rustc (lifetimes are inferred when none are written) but the bootstrap instantiates S as `S<'{region error}, '{region error}, {type error}>` and codegen refuses with `monomorphization resulted in errors: Canonicalizer<'{region error}, '{region error}, {type error}>`. Reproducer: `use std::marker::PhantomData; struct S<'a, 'b, M>(&'a (), &'b (), PhantomData<M>); struct Mode; impl<'a, 'b, M> S<'a, 'b, M> { fn size() -> usize { std::mem::size_of::<M>() } } fn main() { assert_eq!(S::<Mode>::size(), 0); }`. v2 worked around it by writing `Canonicalizer::<'_, '_, M>` at its 4 call sites; the fix belongs in the bootstrap path lowering (rustc: when no lifetime args are given, all are inferred and type args start at the first type param).

history.note: v2's front end follows rustc here: lower/path.rs substs_from_args_and_bindings infers a lifetime met by a type arg (fresh region var in inferred_kind), and infer/path.rs resolve_ty_assoc_item gives the impl fresh args unified with S<'_, '_, Mode>. The bootstrap (blaze-discr) is an older copy; its fix is outside blaze-v2. Pinned in v2 by a new test, hir-ty tests/elided_lifetime_args.rs (your reproducer without std): if it fails in your test run, send it back to db. The 4 Canonicalizer::<'_, '_, M> workarounds can go once the bootstrap is v2
